rv.q: Too often, though, Grandiloquent suffers from precisely the things Gulman is most worried about proving.
There is an honesty in Gulman's writing that in the midst of all the laughs there's a gnawing pain that can stop us dead in our tracks.
Gulman masterfully weaves his insecurities and highly evolved sense of humor into a bravura performance that's as wise as it is hysterical.
Gulman provides a hilariously deadpan account of his young years that proves as poignant as it is funny.
Grandiloquent, his whip-smart, witty, and surprisingly moving show marking his Off-Broadway debut
Gulman's gentle, brainy style of humor will find a receptive audience
